_about: Flow Wolf: Theurge — Ways batch 1: Balance, Confluence, Endurance, Lightning. Mechanics carried over from the SW5E Consular archetypes; every line of text is Bad Eden's own. Built by tools/build-packs.mjs.
_unsure: Standing Wave: the barrier's hit points are tracked as the feature's uses (2 × level + casting mod), as the SW5E data did.
Take and Give: the SW5E doc had a heal (temp HP) activity; the build tool has no heal activity type, so it is a special-activation utility with the formula in the text.
Borne Up: 'kinetic and energy' resistance rendered as bludgeoning/piercing/slashing + lightning; AC 13 + Con and the +level HP are Active Effects using @ roll data.

Live Wire: SW5E's 'shocked' condition does not exist in D&D; rendered as 'jolted: can't take reactions until the start of your next turn'. Uses are 2 flat (the +1 at 5/9/13/17 is in the text; subclasses have no scale values in the tool yet).
Nothing Held Back: 'true damage' rendered as damage that can't be reduced or prevented.

subclasses.name: Way of Balance
subclasses.description: There is a quiet in the middle of the river, and the Way of Balance lives there. These Theurges don't want the fight to be fair; they want it level, and they use the Flow to make it so: a wall around the people they stand with, a hand on the throat of anyone else's power.

subclasses.name: Way of Confluence
subclasses.description: Everything alive is wet with the same water. The Way of Confluence learns where one creek runs into the next and puts a hand on the join: to keep a friend breathing with what an enemy no longer needs, or the other way round, depending on the day.

subclasses.name: Way of Endurance
subclasses.description: Some Theurges point the Flow at the world. The Way of Endurance points it inward and lets it set, like concrete. They get hit a great deal, and the strange thing is how little it seems to matter, and how much of it comes back out again.

subclasses.name: Way of Lightning
subclasses.description: Of all the things the Flow does when it runs downstream, nothing draws a crowd like lightning. The Way of Lightning pulls raw current out of the air and throws it, and what it leaves behind is shaking, smoking, and usually not interested in a second round.

features.name: Standing Wave
features.description:
Way of Balance, 3rd level

You can stand a wave up around yourself and leave it standing. When you cast an Unaligned power of 1st level or higher, you can raise a barrier on yourself at the same time. It lasts until you finish a long rest. The barrier has hit points equal to twice your Theurge level + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice), and it can never have more than that.

Whenever you take damage, the barrier takes it instead. If that damage drops the barrier to 0 hit points, you take whatever is left over.

At 0 hit points the barrier can't absorb anything, but it hasn't gone anywhere. Whenever you cast an Unaligned power of 1st level or higher, the barrier regains hit points equal to twice the power's level.

Once you raise the barrier, you can't raise it again until you finish a long rest. (Track the barrier's hit points as this feature's uses.)

features.name: Thrown Wave
features.description:
Way of Balance, 6th level

The wave doesn't have to stay on you. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to put your Standing Wave in the way, and the barrier takes the damage instead. If that drops the barrier to 0 hit points, the creature takes whatever is left over.

features.name: Ripple
features.description:
Way of Balance, 10th level

Even the small stuff feeds the wave. When you cast an at-will Unaligned power, your Standing Wave regains 1 hit point. You can't bring the barrier above half its maximum hit points this way.

features.name: Steady Hand
features.description:
Way of Balance, 14th level

Other people's power is just more water, and you know how to put your hand in it. When you cast a power that calls for an ability check as part of casting it, such as @UUID[{{uuid:powers:sever-the-current}}]{Sever the Current} or @UUID[{{uuid:powers:stilling}}]{Stilling}, add your proficiency bonus to that check.

features.name: Still Water
features.description:
Way of Balance, 18th level

Nobody's current moves you much any more. You have advantage on saving throws against powers, and you have resistance to the damage powers deal.

features.name: Take and Give
features.description:
Way of Confluence, 3rd level

Where one life ends or starts again, some of it runs over into you. When a power you cast drops a hostile creature to 0 hit points, or brings a creature back from 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to half your Theurge level (rounded down) + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

features.name: Empowered Connection
features.description:
Way of Confluence, 6th level

Borrowed life makes a better conductor. While you have temporary hit points, add half your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) to any damage or healing you do with a power, unless the power already includes that modifier.

features.name: Not Today
features.description:
Way of Confluence, 10th level

You've got a hand on the join, and you're not letting go of your own. When you're reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can spend 5 Flow points to drop to 1 hit point instead.

features.name: Two Birds
features.description:
Way of Confluence, 14th level

Two creeks, one hand. When you cast a power of 5th level or lower that deals damage or restores hit points and targets only one creature, you can have it target two creatures instead, as long as both are in range and within 5 feet of each other.

You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all spent uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Dynamic Attachment
features.description:
Way of Confluence, 18th level

Borrowed life is armor, and it is also a knife. While you have temporary hit points, you have resistance to the damage powers deal, and the powers you cast ignore resistance.

features.name: Borne Up
features.description:
Way of Endurance, 3rd level

The current runs through your bones and sets there. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your hit point maximum increases by 3, and by 1 more every time you gain a level in this class.
  • Your base AC is 13 + your Constitution modifier.
  • When you make a melee weapon attack as part of a power you cast, you can use Wisdom or Charisma (your choice) instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls.

Also, as an action, you can gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, slashing, and lightning damage for 1 minute. It ends early if you end it as a bonus action, if you're incapacitated, or if you put on armor other than a shield. You can do this twice, and you regain all spent uses when you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Retaliation Strike
features.description:
Way of Endurance, 6th level

What goes in comes back out. When you deal damage with a power or a melee weapon attack, if you've taken damage since the start of your last turn, you deal an extra 1d6 damage of the same type as the power or weapon.

The die grows as you gain levels in this class: 1d8 at 9th level, 1d10 at 13th, and 1d12 at 17th.

features.name: Boundless Vitality
features.description:
Way of Endurance, 10th level

You've learned to pour it back in as fast as it leaks. When you take damage, as long as it wouldn't reduce you to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction and spend 1 Flow point to regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

The die grows as you gain levels in this class: 1d10 at 13th level and 1d12 at 17th.

features.name: Unrelenting Resilience
features.description:
Way of Endurance, 14th level

When you use Boundless Vitality while concentrating on a power, you can add the number you rolled to the Constitution saving throw you make to keep concentration.

Also, when you're reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright while your Borne Up resistance is active, you can drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you do, you can't do it again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Flood
features.description:
Way of Endurance, 18th level

Everything you've been holding, let go at once. As an action, choose a point within 60 feet of you. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of that point must make a Constitution saving throw against your Unaligned power save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 force damage and gains 1 level of exhaustion. On a success, it takes half the damage and no exhaustion.

For each creature that fails, one friendly creature within 30 feet of it can regain hit points equal to the damage dealt. A friendly creature can benefit from this only once per turn.

You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of once), and you regain all spent uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Live Wire
features.description:
Way of Lightning, 3rd level

Lightning doesn't care which bank you cast from. When you cast a power that deals lightning damage, you can use Wisdom or Charisma as your casting ability for it.

Also, when you cast a damage-dealing power that calls for a power attack or a saving throw, you can make it deal lightning damage instead. If the power calls for a saving throw other than Dexterity, it calls for a Dexterity saving throw instead. If you hit, or a target fails its save, each affected creature is jolted until the start of your next turn: it can't take reactions.

You can do this twice. You gain one more use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level, and you regain all spent uses when you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Potent Lightning
features.description:
Way of Lightning, 6th level

Add your casting ability modifier (minimum of +1) to any damage you deal with a power that deals lightning damage, unless the power already includes that modifier.

features.name: Blistering Rebuke
features.description:
Way of Lightning, 10th level

Touch the wire, learn about the wire. When a creature you can see within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to make it roll a Dexterity saving throw against your Unaligned power save DC. On a failed save, it takes 1d10 + your Theurge level lightning damage, is pushed 10 feet away from you, and is jolted until the end of its next turn (it can't take reactions). On a success, it takes half the damage and isn't moved or jolted.

You can do this four times. You gain one more use at 13th and 17th level, and you regain all spent uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Grounded
features.description:
Way of Lightning, 14th level

You have resistance to lightning damage, and the powers you cast ignore resistance to lightning damage.

features.name: Nothing Held Back
features.description:
Way of Lightning, 18th level

You can open the tap all the way on your plainer lightning. When you cast a power of 1st through 6th level that deals lightning damage, you can have it deal maximum damage.

You can do this safely a number of times equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of once). Past that, before you finish a long rest, each use costs you: immediately after you cast the power, you take 2d12 damage per level of the power, and that damage can't be reduced or prevented. Every further use before a long rest adds 1d12 to the damage.
